answer: One concrete sybil resistance is a canyon-gated spiral of sparrow probes: each new identity must complete a chain of 12 sequential lightweight verification tasks whose difficulty multiplies by 1.3 per step, seeded by the prior checkpoint so they cannot be precomputed in parallel. An attacker minting n identities pays the full spiral cost for each, totaling roughly n times 12 times average probe cost, and any failed probe burns a small bond; the canyon isolates funding roots so shared compute does not amortize across clones.
